13: Things to know before you start
14: THE "PRICE INCLUDES SALES TAX?" COLUMN IS WHAT MAKES THE TOTAL WORK. US dealers list prices before sales tax and the tax only shows up on the invoice; some quotes include it and some spec sheets don't say. Adding up the two kinds of price throws the investment off, and nobody notices because the total looks "reasonable". Here each line declares its basis and the sheet brings them all to pre-tax before adding up; your sales tax rate goes in "Settings", and in the US it's a cost.
15: WHAT HAS NO PUBLISHED PRICE IS MARKED "ASSUMPTION". The retarder-proofer, cold storage, fixtures, POS, packaging, security deposit and working capital aren't sold from a catalog: they're quoted. The cell comes with a default value so the workbook works from the first minute, and the "Published range" column tells you whether there's any reference range and where it comes from. Get three quotes and replace it.
16: A TAKEOVER'S ASKING PRICE ISN'T WHAT A TAKEOVER COSTS. The listings you collect are ASKING prices, not prices paid, and none of them comes with its P&L. They're for seeing the range and negotiating, never for valuing a business.
17: WORKING CAPITAL IS PART OF THE INVESTMENT. Four months of fixed costs in the bank the day you open isn't caution: it's the difference between riding out the ramp-up and closing in month eight with a business that works. It goes inside startup costs, and that's why this workbook's total is higher than any build-out and equipment quote.
18: THE SECURITY DEPOSIT ISN'T AN EXPENSE, AND PACKAGING ISN'T AN INVESTMENT EITHER. The first is money you get back; the second is inventory. You need both the day you sign, so they're in startup costs, but they're left out of the comparison with published build-out and equipment figures: otherwise you'd be comparing two different things.
